title: Domestic datacentres reduce home heating costs by £180 annually
summary:
A London homeowner has reduced hot water bills by up to £15 monthly using a domestic datacentre system that converts computer processing heat into usable energy. The technology, installed in 100 UK homes with 3,000 on waiting lists, aims to provide 80% of household hot water heating needs.

title: Government launches register to tackle rogue builders
summary:
The government has launched a register of trusted traders and a payment app this month aimed at protecting homeowners from fraudulent builders. According to Citizens Advice, 4.8 million homeowners experienced problems with home repair jobs in the previous 18 months, with 1.7 million losing an average of £750 each.

title: Recognise Bank completes £2m bridge loan in two weeks
summary:
Recognise Bank has provided a £2.025 million bridging loan to refinance existing debt on a residential development site in Hertfordshire, completing the transaction within two weeks of initial enquiry. The 12-month facility was arranged at 60% loan-to-value for a property developer with over 30 years of experience.

title: Architecturally distinct homes listed across England
summary:
Five architecturally distinctive properties have been listed across England, priced between £495,000 and £850,000. The homes range from a converted 1909 iron chapel to a 2023 Passivhaus-certified build, reflecting varied architectural approaches in the current residential market.

title: Building society funds £54,000 SPV mortgage for first-time landlords
summary:
Darlington Building Society has completed a £54,000 limited company buy-to-let mortgage at 80% loan-to-value for two first-time landlords purchasing through a newly formed special purpose vehicle. The transaction involved borrowers with no previous landlord experience who were non-owner-occupiers entering the property investment market.

title: UK property sales fall 7.3% year-on-year amid rising fall-throughs
summary:
UK property sales fell 7.3% year-on-year to 874,000 homes sold subject to contract through week 36 of 2026. Only 55% of homes leaving agents' books in August exchanged and completed, below the seven-year average of 57.6%.

title: Estate agents underutilise CRM databases, survey finds
summary:
Estate agencies may be overlooking potential business opportunities within their existing customer relationship management systems, according to new research. A survey found that 82.4% of agency leaders believe their databases contain untapped revenue potential.

title: Norwich estate agency relocates after acquisition
summary:
Independent estate agency Pymm and Co has relocated its Norwich headquarters to larger premises following the acquisition of a rival lettings firm. The agency has moved from Ber Street to 46 Rose Lane after 20 years at its former office.

title: Estate agency job vacancies reach 1,300 across England
summary:
Estate agency job vacancies in England have reached approximately 1,300, with London accounting for nearly one-third of all advertised positions. The data contrasts with recent figures showing overall headcount in the sector has fallen sharply over the past year.

title: AI property research risks costly errors, buying agents warn
summary:
Property buyers relying on artificial intelligence platforms for purchasing decisions risk making costly errors due to flawed data and misleading analysis, according to a buying agent. Rob Fanshawe, partner at Property Vision, has warned that whilst AI has provided buyers with rapid access to property information, the technology's limitations could result in financial mistakes running into thousands of pounds.
